tagline: Big, loud capital that most travellers only pass through
summary: Guatemala City is the country's sprawling capital and the hub for onward buses, with a historic centre (Zona 1) and a modern Zona 10 and Zona 4. The vibe is busy and urban, with most backpackers staying one night before heading to Antigua, Flores or the border.
things_to_do: Palacio Nacional and Plaza de la Constitucion in Zona 1
Museo Popol Vuh and Museo Ixchel
Day trip to Antigua or Pacaya

tagline: Colonial town under three volcanoes
summary: Antigua is a cobbled UNESCO colonial town and the main backpacker base in Guatemala, ringed by Agua, Fuego and Acatenango volcanoes. Compact, walkable and very touristy, with language students, cafes, rooftop bars and a dense shuttle network.
things_to_do: Arch of Santa Catalina and Parque Central
Colonial ruins (Capuchinas, San Francisco el Grande)

tagline: Volcano lake of Maya villages, better for relaxing than partying
summary: Lake Atitlan is a deep volcanic lake ringed by villages, each with its own character: Panajachel is the gateway, San Pedro is the backpacker and party base, San Marcos and Santa Cruz are yoga and chill spots. Boats (lanchas) link everything, and the pace is slow.
things_to_do: Climb San Pedro or Atitlan volcano
Kayak or dive from Santa Cruz La Laguna
Visit Santiago Atitlan and the Maximon shrine

tagline: Highland university city with Spanish schools and volcano hikes
summary: Quetzaltenango (Xela) is Guatemala's second city, a working highland town with far fewer tourists than Antigua. The vibe is local and student-driven, with cheap Spanish schools, hot springs and a base for volcano treks.

tagline: Lake-island town and gateway to Tikal
summary: Flores is a small, colourful island in Lake Peten Itza linked by a causeway, and the base for Tikal, the Belize border and long bus legs. Relaxed and walkable, with lakeside bars and sunsets, and many people leave at 4am for Tikal sunrise.
things_to_do: Tikal ruins at sunrise or sunset
Swim and sunset at the lake
Cave and cenote day trips (Actun Kan)
Walk the island and its lakefront bars

tagline: Jungle river hostels at the gate of Semuc Champey
summary: Lanquin is a small village in the Alta Verapaz hills and the base for Semuc Champey's turquoise limestone pools. Hostels sit along the river in the jungle, with a social, party-leaning backpacker crowd and rough minibus access.
things_to_do: Swim the Semuc Champey pools and walk to the mirador
Hostel river swings and communal dinners

tagline: Buzzing Central American capital with a growing food and museum scene
summary: San Salvador is a bustling, polarised capital of malls, nightlife and gritty districts, ringed by volcanoes. Most travellers use it as a hub and spend a day or two on museums, pupusas and viewpoints before heading to the coast.
things_to_do: Los Planes de Renderos viewpoint and pupusas

hostels.name: Hostal Cumbres del Volcan Flor Blanca

tagline: Small surf village with sunset rock and weekend parties
summary: El Tunco is a tiny black-sand surf village on El Salvador's Pacific coast, busy with backpackers and Salvadoran weekenders. El Zonte, a few km along the coast, is the quieter surf and Bitcoin-beach alternative.
things_to_do: Learn to surf at El Sunzal, La Bocana or Bocanita
Weekend live music and bar crawl

tagline: Calm Maya-ruins town with a famous hieroglyphic stairway
summary: Copan Ruinas is a small, relaxed Honduran hill town of cobbled, colourful streets beside one of the best Maya sites in the region. Easy walking, coffee, birds and hot springs, with a mellow backpacker crowd.
things_to_do: Copan archaeological park and Hieroglyphic Stairway
Tea and chocolate tasting in town

tagline: Industrial Honduran hub, a transit stop
summary: San Pedro Sula is Honduras' commercial centre and the main bus and air hub for the north coast and Copan. It is a working city with little for visitors beyond onward connections.

tagline: Hilly colonial capital, mostly a transit point
summary: Tegucigalpa is a sprawling hillside capital with a small colonial core, steep stone streets and big city views. Few travellers stay long, but it is the link for Nicaragua and the south.
things_to_do: Catedral de San Miguel Arcangel and Parque Central

tagline: Caribbean port city and ferry gateway to the Bay Islands
summary: La Ceiba is a friendly, laid-back Caribbean port city and the departure point for ferries to Roatan and Utila. It also works as a base for rafting and national parks.
things_to_do: White-water rafting on the Cangrejal river

tagline: Largest Bay Island, diving and beaches at higher prices
summary: Roatan is the biggest of Honduras' Bay Islands, with diving, snorkelling and white-sand beaches, plus cruise-ship traffic at the resort end. West End is the backpacker base and West Bay the best beach, and it is pricier than the mainland.
things_to_do: Roatan Brewing Co. and rum tasting

tagline: Backpacker dive island with cheap certification
summary: Utila is the smallest and cheapest of the Bay Islands, a low-key Caribbean dive island with a social backpacker scene. Most people come to learn to dive and stay longer than planned.
things_to_do: Snorkel and swim at Chepes Beach

tagline: Sprawling lakeside capital, mainly a transit stop
summary: Managua is Nicaragua's spread-out capital on Lake Managua, without a real centre, and most travellers move straight on to Granada or Leon. Hot, busy and car-oriented.
things_to_do: Old cathedral ruins and Plaza de la Revolucion
Onward day trip to Masaya volcano

tagline: Revolutionary university city and volcano-boarding base
summary: Leon is a hot, intellectual colonial city of grand churches, murals and student bars. A popular backpacker stop with cheap beds, and it is where people go to board down Cerro Negro.
things_to_do: Rooftop of the Cathedral of Leon
Day trip to Las Penitas beach

tagline: Colourful colonial city on Lake Nicaragua
summary: Granada is Nicaragua's pastel colonial showpiece beside Lake Nicaragua, with a lively pedestrian street, plazas and many hostels. Tourist-oriented but relaxed, and the base for Masaya and Mombacho.
things_to_do: Calle La Calzada bars and restaurants
Isletas boat trip on Lake Nicaragua
Climb the Cathedral or La Merced tower

tagline: Pacific surf town and Sunday Funday party hub
summary: San Juan del Sur is a beach town in a horseshoe bay, with surf camps, sunset hill views and a big party scene. The most tourist-focused place in Nicaragua, with a large expat crowd.
things_to_do: Surf lessons at Playa Maderas or Hermosa

tagline: Twin-volcano island in Lake Nicaragua with slow rural life
summary: Ometepe is a figure-eight island formed by Concepcion and Maderas volcanoes in Lake Nicaragua. Farms, jungle lodges and beaches give it a slow, outdoorsy vibe, and travel across it is by bus or scooter.
things_to_do: Kayak or SUP at Charco Verde

tagline: Quiet Caribbean island with Creole culture
summary: Big Corn Island is the larger and more developed of the two Corn Islands, quiet, English-Creole in character and good for relaxing, snorkelling and sunsets. It is the arrival point by plane or panga from the mainland.

tagline: Car-free barefoot Caribbean island
summary: Little Corn is a one-square-mile island with no cars, sandy paths, simple lodges and a small but lively social scene. Remote and basic, with limited hot water and electricity.
things_to_do: Yoga at Firefly or the Lighthouse

tagline: Costa Rican capital, mainly a hub
summary: San Jose is a busy highland capital with a handful of museums and markets, mostly used as a hub for buses and flights. Not a highlight in itself, but it has a decent hostel scene.
things_to_do: Day trip to Poas or Irazu volcano

tagline: Dry-forest gateway city to Guanacaste beaches and the Nicaragua border
summary: Liberia is a hot, practical town in Guanacaste with an international airport, used as a base for beaches, volcano parks and the Penas Blancas crossing. Quiet, with a few hostels.
things_to_do: Rincon de la Vieja national park
Day trip to Santa Rosa national park

tagline: Skyline capital with a colonial old quarter and the Canal
summary: Panama City mixes a glass skyline, the Panama Canal and the restored Casco Viejo old quarter with rooftop bars. The main arrival hub in the region and base for the San Blas and Colombia routes.
things_to_do: Miraflores Locks on the Panama Canal
Cinta Costera and Mercado de Mariscos

tagline: Guna-run island archipelago of white-sand cays
summary: San Blas (Guna Yala) is an autonomous Guna territory of about 365 small islands on Panama's Caribbean coast. Stays are basic cabins or sailing trips, with no ATMs, and Guna culture and molas are central.
things_to_do: Visit a Guna community and buy molas

tagline: Roadless Caribbean village on the Colombia-Panama border
summary: Capurgana is a small, car-free village in Choco reached only by boat or plane, with jungle trails and calm bays, and the usual stepping stone for Darien crossings. Quiet and low-key.
things_to_do: Walk the jungle trails to El Cielito waterfall
Snorkel at La Mocha and Playa Aguacate
Boat or walk to Sapzurro and La Miel

tagline: Rainforest bay for Corcovado wildlife and Caño Island diving
summary: A calm, remote bay on Costa Rica's Osa Peninsula, reached by boat from Sierpe or a small plane. Base for guided hikes into Corcovado National Park (scarlet macaws, rare mammals) and for diving or snorkelling at Isla del Caño, with white-tip reef sharks, turtles and rays.
things_to_do: Two-tank dive at Isla del Caño
Whale and dolphin spotting by boat
